metadata.note: The Sullivan Railroad (Sullivan County Railroad from 1866), Bellows Falls VT - Charlestown - Claremont Junction - Windsor VT, 24.3 owned miles all in New Hampshire on the east bank of the Connecticut plus 0.7 mi of Central Vermont track into Windsor. Opened 1849 as the link between the Cheshire at Bellows Falls and the Vermont Central at Windsor. One physical line drawn as one feature per operator era on identical geometry (CLAUDE.md Rule 4 splits): Sullivan Railroad 1849-1861, Vermont Valley 1861-1866, Vermont Central 1866-1872, Central Vermont 1873-1876, Connecticut River Railroad 1880-1892, Boston and Maine 1893-1966. Built from research/branches/sullivan_county_railroad.txt (researched 2026-10-15).
omitted: 1877-1880: passenger service almost certainly continued, but no source names who ran the trains (ICC says only 'various lessees' to 31 Aug 1880; candidates are the Central Vermont, the Northern RR of NH, or the Vermont Valley of 1871). Left undrawn rather than coloured with a guessed company.
Amtrak (Montrealer 1972-1987 and 1989-1995, Vermonter from 1995): already drawn as amtrak-90 in amtrak.geojson; not duplicated.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Built to Rule 1: the B&M feature ends with passenger service in 1966; post-1966 freight (B&M, Central Vermont, New England Central) is mentioned in notes only. The Springfield Terminal Railway (Charlestown NH - Springfield VT, electric, passengers 1897-1947 per Fowler, freight-only by 1951) is a separate company and not drawn here.
not_yet_sourced: Who ran the trains 1851-1861, after the bondholders' trustees took the property on 29 Sept 1851 (drawn under the Sullivan Railroad name with that caveat).

The 1861-1866 Vermont Valley lease rests on de.Wikipedia only (Lindsell 2000, Jones 1993); and the Vermont Valley was itself leased to Rutland & Burlington interests from 1 June 1865, so the 1865-1866 operator may differ.

The 1876-1880 operator (see omitted). SOURCE CONFLICT: de.Wikipedia ends the Central Vermont lease in 1876; en.Wikipedia 'Bellows Falls station' implies the CV still held it 'by 1880'. ICC Valuation Reports vol. 30 (Google Books GO1DAAAAIAAJ) or Lindsell's Rail Lines of Northern New England would likely settle it.
Opening day to Windsor: 5 Feb 1849 (de.Wikipedia CV), 6 Feb 1849 construction completion (ICC), 'the next month' (en.Wikipedia), 31 March 1849 (Tuttle). Year firm.
Year the river bridge into Bellows Falls was built ('a year or two' after Jan 1849 per Tuttle).
Day of the 1966 end: 6 Sept (en.Wikipedia) vs 3/4 Sept. Year firm.
All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates; no pre-1951 timetable was read for frequency.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, February 1952 (schedules of Sept 1951), Boston and Maine Table 16 'Connecticut River Line' and station index (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt in the site repository)

geometry_source: OpenStreetMap route relation 9048140 (New England Central Railroad; on Bellows Falls - Windsor its ways are tagged old_railway_operator=B&M) -- https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/9048140
properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap: shortest-path routing (opstrace.py) over the New England Central Railroad's active track, all 24 NECR ways on this stretch being members of OSM route relation 9048140 and tagged old_railway_operator=B&M. Traced 24.9 mi Bellows Falls station - Windsor station, 100% on B&M-tagged ways, against a documented 25.0-25.1 mi (ICC valuation: 24.308 mi owned, all in New Hampshire, plus 0.726 mi of Central Vermont track from the river bridge into Windsor; John Fowler's mileposts 84.0 to 109.1 = 25.1 mi). No straight-line approximation. Cut at Bellows Falls station (the line crosses the Connecticut into New Hampshire immediately north of it) and at Windsor station (recrossing into Vermont about 0.7 mi south of the station), which is where cheshire_railroad.geojson / amtrak-90 and vermont_central_railroad.geojson meet it. CAVEAT (CLAUDE.md Rule 2): this is the MODERN alignment drawn back to 1849. In particular, per the 1929 Tuttle history quoting the Bellows Falls Gazette, the railroad bridge into Bellows Falls was not built until 'a year or two' after the January 1849 opening, so for roughly 1849-1850/51 Sullivan trains met the Cheshire on the New Hampshire bank (Walpole / North Walpole) and did not enter Bellows Falls; the first ~0.3 mi at the Bellows Falls end is therefore a later alignment for those years. The second main track (17.07 mi, built 1884-1903 per ICC) and any 19th-century realignments have not been backed out, and no period valuation map was consulted.

segments.note: The Sullivan Railroad (NH charter 10 July 1846) opened to Charlestown with an excursion on 1 January 1849 and a ceremonial opening on Thursday 4 January 1849 (Bellows Falls Gazette, quoted in Tuttle 1929), and through to Windsor in February-March 1849 -- sources conflict on the day: 5 Feb (de.Wikipedia Central Vermont), 'completed February 6, 1849' (ICC valuation, a construction date), 'the next month' (en.Wikipedia Bellows Falls station), 31 March (Tuttle). The year is firm. The company ran its own trains with its own superintendent (Edward Thompson) and conductors, headquartered at Charlestown, as the link in the 1849 Boston - Fitchburg - Cheshire - Sullivan - Vermont Central through route to Burlington. Until the river bridge into Bellows Falls was built 'a year or two later' (Tuttle), trains met the Cheshire on the New Hampshire bank. Ends 1851 only because the bondholders' trustees took the property on 29 Sept 1851 (ICC); service continued. Headway is an estimate: no timetable for this era was read for frequency.
sources: Segment-level: start 1849 from the Bellows Falls Gazette of 4 Jan 1849 as quoted in Tuttle (1929), the ICC valuation report ('completed February 6, 1849'), en.Wikipedia 'Bellows Falls station' and de.Wikipedia; 1851 = ICC date of surrender to the bondholders' trustees. Fowler's 1850 Pathfinder column (x) lists all stations. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: From 29 Sept 1851 the property was held by the trustees of the Sullivan Railroad's bondholders (ICC). WHO RAN THE TRAINS 1851-1861 IS NOT ESTABLISHED -- drawn under the Sullivan name because it was the same company's property in its trustees' hands and no other operator is named; it may instead have been worked by the trustees directly or by a connecting road. Passenger service itself is not in doubt: Fowler's 1850 Pathfinder column shows the stations, and the line was the only rail link between the Vermont Central and the roads south. Ends with the Vermont Valley Railroad lease of September 1861 (de.Wikipedia, citing Lindsell 2000 and Jones 1993). Headway is an estimate: no timetable for this era was read for frequency.
sources: Segment-level: continuity from Fowler (1850 Pathfinder stations); 1851 from the ICC valuation (trustees, 29 Sept 1851); 1861 end from de.Wikipedia 'Sullivan County Railroad' and 'Vermont Valley Railroad' only (single secondary chain). The operator for these years is NOT SOURCED. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: The Vermont Valley Railroad (Brattleboro - Bellows Falls) leased the Sullivan Railroad in September 1861; the lease was dissolved in 1866 (de.Wikipedia, citing Lindsell 2000 and Jones 1993 -- not independently confirmed). Caveat: the Vermont Valley was itself leased from 1 June 1865 for ten years to Rutland & Burlington interests (de.Wikipedia), so for 1865-1866 the trains may have been run by those lessees. Service continuity is not in doubt; only the operator is. The Sullivan property was sold to a bondholders' committee on 20 July 1866 and reincorporated as the Sullivan County Railroad (NH act of 3 July 1866). Headway is an estimate: no timetable for this era was read for frequency.
sources: NOT SOURCED AT SEGMENT LEVEL: the 1861 lease and its 1866 dissolution rest only on de.Wikipedia (two articles drawing on the same books, Lindsell 2000 and Jones 1993); nothing independent has been checked against this segment's operator, years or headway.

segments.note: Leased to the Vermont Central from 7 September 1866 (ICC: 'various lessees operated the property from September 7, 1866, to August 31, 1880'; de.Wikipedia names the Vermont Central as lessee from 1866). This was the Vermont Central's southern outlet: its Windsor - Burlington main line connected here for Boston (via the Cheshire) and New York (via the Vermont Valley). The company was renamed the Central Vermont Railroad on 2 Nov 1872; the split into a separate feature from 1873 follows the colour convention already in vermont_central_railroad.geojson, not an operator change. Headway is an estimate: no timetable for this era was read for frequency.
sources: Segment-level: start 7 Sept 1866 from the ICC valuation and de.Wikipedia (Sullivan County RR; Central Vermont 'von 1866 bis 1876'); 1872 end = the Nov 2 1872 rename as recorded in vermont_central_railroad.geojson. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Operated by the Connecticut River Railroad under a 50-year agency agreement of 31 August 1880 (ICC); the CRR controlled the Vermont Valley (99% of its stock), which bought the Sullivan County Railroad's stock from the Northern Railroad of New Hampshire on 1 Oct 1880 (de.Wikipedia). Springfield - Bellows Falls - Windsor became one through route; the second main track was begun in 1884 (ICC). Central Vermont through trains also ran over the line by trackage rights. Ends when the agreement was assigned to the Boston and Maine on 1 January 1893 (ICC). Headway is an estimate: no timetable for this era was read for frequency.
sources: Segment-level: start 31 Aug 1880 and end (assignment to B&M 1 Jan 1893) from the ICC valuation report; 1880 stock purchase from de.Wikipedia. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Boston and Maine's Connecticut River Line (Springfield - White River Junction, over the Central Vermont north of Windsor), operated by the B&M from 1 January 1893 when the Connecticut River RR's agency agreement was assigned to it (ICC); the B&M's direct lease of 1 Jan 1925 and 1949 merger did not change who ran the trains. The September 1951 Official Guide (Table 16) shows rail times at Charlestown, Claremont Junction and Windsor, including Washington/New York - Montreal through trains (the Montrealer/Washingtonian, drawn separately in montrealer.geojson). Fowler's B&M public timetables: West Claremont and Balloch last listed 1921, South and North Charlestown 1932, Charlestown and Claremont Junction still 1953. Passenger service to Bellows Falls ended in September 1966 -- 6 Sept per en.Wikipedia 'Bellows Falls station', 3/4 Sept for the last Montrealer/Washingtonian per other research; year firm. Freight continued (B&M, later Central Vermont and New England Central) and is not drawn; Amtrak's Montrealer restored passenger trains from 30 Sept 1972 and is drawn as amtrak-90 in amtrak.geojson. Headway is an estimate: no timetable for this era was read for frequency.
sources: Segment-level: 1893 start from the ICC valuation (assignment of the agency agreement to the B&M); service in 1951 from the Official Guide Feb 1952 Table 16 and station index; Fowler's 1906/1921/1932/1953 B&M timetable columns; 1966 end from en.Wikipedia 'Bellows Falls station' and The Commons. Headway not sourced (Guide OCR too damaged to count trains).
